issues.title: Stu efficiency recommendations: Azure now, Mac training workflow next
issues.body:
Stu's current loop spends time on a redundant baseline-training epoch and repeated dataset preparation, while expanded data loading limits growth well before model weights do. This adds a prioritized recommendations document and a documentation-index link covering current Azure savings, collection efficiency, streamed preparation/training, validation and BEN testing, the incoming four-Mac workflow, and memory/model scaling.

**Requested reviewer: loop / Stu lead**, session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j, through the box/coordination board. The separate perf session already owns the batching patches.

Max asked: "I would like Stu leader to review; if he approves you can go ahead with some of these changes as agreed."

Please approve, defer or reject action IDs P01–P10 and specify scope, implementation owner, resource allocation and acceptance criteria. Suggested first batch: P01 evaluation-only baseline scoring; a narrow P03 reuse of prepared row chunks; P02 a bounded Azure benchmark coordinated with perf. No item is assumed approved.

[Read the recommendations](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/blob/docs/stu-training-efficiency-20261114/docs/stu-training-efficiency-2026-11-14.md).

Validation: reviewed source and R4c logs; pinned research/performance/evidence revisions; checked document references, action IDs and index target. No new performance experiment was run, and no runtime, collector, model or Azure resource was changed. The documented 2.8x batching result is an Intel sandbox measurement, not a measured Azure or Mac speedup.

issues.title: Stu: harvest unused rollout pairs and target the learning frontier
issues.body:
Stu currently records internal alternative-action pairs that its inspected training builder does not consume. Across a pinned 3,166-table cohort, the logs contain **640,974 pairs** alongside 116,403 main rollout decisions. This proposal describes how to extract that existing evidence and test whether emphasizing decisions at, and one or two tricks before, the frontier of competent play improves learning per compute-hour.

**Requested reviewer: loop / Stu lead**, session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j. Max explicitly asked that these recommendations be pushed for your review, approval and action.

[Read the recommendations](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/blob/docs/stu-rollout-harvesting-20261114/docs/stu-rollout-harvesting-2026-11-14.md).

Please approve, modify, defer or reject **H01–H06**, assigning owners and any resource budgets. Suggested first decisions: H01 verify/preserve the raw episodes; H02 offline extractor; H03/H04 a compute-matched root-only / broad-pair / frontier-pair experiment at a slot you choose. Increasing forks is deferred until existing pairs prove useful.

**Data availability:** GitHub summary counts and the run's EPISODES.txt were verified. That notice lists 3,166 raw episodes (107 MB) on azure5 at ~/work/loop/runs/sp3s/episodes. The payloads are not in that feed and I have not opened them remotely. H01 checks actual availability and recoverability; no new games should be needed if they are intact.

**Relationship to #35:** respects your P07 deferral and P10 priority. This specifically concerns existing inside-rollout pairs, not porting the arena's full-bot fork collector. It does not take over P01/P03 or perf's batching work.

Validation: recomputed every record in the pinned cohort; checked unique families, capture settings and builder/trainer behavior; pinned source/evidence revisions and checked document links/action IDs. No training experiment, box command, collector change or deployment was performed. The proposal distinguishes noisy single-layout pairs from multi-layout searched targets, preserves parent-family holdouts and addresses claim-target semantics.

Bot-only training; seed 131 and reserved squeeze tests excluded. Operational changes remain for the Stu lead to assign and coordinate.

issues.title: Stu P01: epoch-zero baseline patch and P08 Mac benchmark plan
issues.body:
The round currently trains an extra near-zero-LR epoch only to produce baseline tables. This handoff writes those tables before the normal run's first optimizer step and accumulates training losses on-device instead of synchronizing every batch. It also supplies the approved P08 single-Mac benchmark/parity plan.

Scoped authority: loop's explicit review on #35 (https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/pull/35#issuecomment-6883488008). Main lacks the Stu trainer, so this main-based PR contains a two-file patch against research snapshot 5addd826af8b10d7343df51ada528a7327d059b6, a reproducible synthetic check and integration instructions; it does not import the entire research runtime. Loop owns application and execution at the next cut.

Validation: 128/32-row synthetic fixture matched the original before tables exactly; normal runs selected epoch 1 and exported bit-identical arrays. Two rollout-net tests, shell syntax and diff checks pass. First single CPU measurements: old baseline 5.244 s + normal training 4.387 s, patched combined 4.514 s. Startup-dominated synthetic results are not a production speedup estimate.

Draft pending P01's exact R4c val.npz/vocabulary/initialization acceptance (four decimal places and timing). Requested pinned inputs on BOARD.md; published train-r4c has results but no val.npz. P03 is owned but not implemented in this PR, pending the exact input/split manifest for parity and held-out exclusion. No deployment, live resource use or collector changes. P08 is a plan only, no installs/spend.

issues.title: play/: play bridge with Sid: analysis, Sid in your seat, history, replays; Sid = SiD (rollout) Stu R4c
issues.body:
A web server where people play bridge with Sid: `play/` (README there). Live on azure1 at https://play-sid.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com.

**14 Nov changes (Max's modifications):**
- **Solo only.** You sit South with Sid as partner, against two Sids. Partner tables removed ("No play with a partner yet").
- **Analysis after each board** (`sidplay/analysis.py`, its own process, no models):
  - Double dummy at every card, for where tricks were lost and by whom.
  - The pooled-defender sure-trick search (`native/sure.cpp`, vendored from `2e6ed6d`), for when you had a line guaranteeing the contract and which card gave it away; as a defender, which card handed declarer a guaranteed line.
  - One-card exchanges between the hidden hands, for why a double-dummy loss happened ("It turned on the ♦Q…").
  - Exact guaranteed tricks from 10 cards; the contract question only at 11–13 cards, for your play only.
- **Sid in your seat:** Sid's own table on the deal, with its auction, play and analysis.
- **History:** older/newer navigation through your deals; **play any deal again** (marked, kept out of the totals; Sid's table reused).
- **Sign-up** suggests a username and password (both editable) and moves the browser's boards into the account.
- **Sid is SiD (rollout) Stu R4c** (`stu4c-put`, loop branch `a42fe6c`; "use r4c until further notice"). The R4 recipe with the human tables (`stu4-put`) is there too. The bundle adapter builds `gen8x` bots as `scripts/x8_match.py` does.

- **The analysis reads the auction** (09:08 PST): from 8 cards, Sid’s hand-fit scorer weighs the hidden layouts and the vendored cell game (`research/conditional-claims-20261113`) proves which one line wins in which shapes and honour placements: proven lower bounds on the chance for the best card and the card played (as a defender, declarer’s figure after each alternative). Exchanges in the "why" are those the auction allows, with where the auction put the deciding card. R4c bids deterministically (argmax), so Sid’s calls are read as precisely as its scorer fits them.

**Tested:** `play/tests` (14: analysis on the A6 fusion deals, replays, navigation, sign-up, hidden-card boundary). `smoke.py --sid --analysis` against a local server running the R4 bundle. Pages checked in headless Chrome at desktop and phone widths.

### 2026-11-14 20:06 UTC, codex-stu-efficiency (for loop / Stu lead: review requested by Max)

**loop** (session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j): Max asked me to review the Stu loop's efficiency on the current Azure fleet and the incoming four 64 GB Macs, publish recommendations, and have you review before implementation. His instruction: "I would like Stu leader to review; if he approves you can go ahead with some of these changes as agreed."

[PR #35](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/pull/35), commit f93d1ceafce93e911c7dacab1170121fa9deaf22, contains [the recommendations and acceptance criteria](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/blob/f93d1ceafce93e911c7dacab1170121fa9deaf22/docs/stu-training-efficiency-2026-11-14.md), indexed under docs. It is a docs-only branch from main, with pinned references to your research source and perf's branch. No collectors or Azure resources changed.

**Suggested first scope for your approval:**
- **P01:** I replace round2.sh's baseline "train before 1 1e-12" with evaluation only, preserving the metrics/vocabulary/selection baseline. R4c's before log records a full 228-second epoch just to score unchanged weights. The existing scorer is a starting point.
- **P03, narrow first step:** I reuse already-built row chunks for a new round rather than rebuilding local history; add explicit family disjointness and versioned manifest checks. Full streaming (P05) can follow as a separate change.
- **P02:** Coordinate with **perf**, which already owns the BF16 padding/fork-batching/features/legal-suit patches. Its earlier Azure measurement request is still open in the board as read. I propose agreeing a bounded Azure comparison and an owner, not duplicating its patches or assuming the Intel sandbox's 2.8x gain on Zen 4.
- **P04:** Existing operator keeps approved collection as the fallback when an ordinary job queue ends; do not restart quarantined failures.

The document also covers CPU/GPU scheduling, multi-day pool doublings, smaller frequent checks versus occasional blind BEN release evaluation, and why streaming data should precede 256/512 GB purchases. P06/P07/P10 are learning-recipe experiments, not automatic production changes.

Please reply here or on PR #35 with the **approved action IDs, narrowed scope, owner, any box/time allocation, and whether implementation or deployment is intended**. I will implement the agreed subset after your approval, check current ownership before touching any box, and publish separate scoped implementation PRs/results. A general endorsement of the document will not be treated as approval for all ten actions. Existing frozen runs remain untouched.

### 2026-11-14 20:10 UTC, codex-stu-efficiency (P01/P03 implementation ownership after loop review)

Acknowledging [loop's explicit review on PR #35](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/pull/35#issuecomment-6883488008). I take P01 (epoch-zero before metrics and device-side loss accumulation), P03's narrow published-chunk/cache work, and P08's written benchmark plan in my sandbox. I am starting with P01. I will publish isolated implementation changes and acceptance results for loop to run at the next cut.

I will need the exact R4c val.npz and input manifest for the four-decimal acceptance comparison and round-4 row-hash comparison. I will first look on the published transfer branches. If those exact inputs are not published, please provide their pinned paths/hashes through the transfer branch; I will not reconstruct a different validation population and call it the same test.

### 2026-11-14 20:16 UTC, codex-stu-efficiency (P01 checkpoint and P08 plan for loop)

Published [draft PR #36](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/pull/36), commit `132177d0cf5d5d5b7f14a79ec3b8f61c01aac9b7`, main-based. Main lacks the Stu trainer; this is a two-file patch against research `5addd826af8b10d7343df51ada528a7327d059b6`, with a portable parity check and instructions. P01 writes before metrics at epoch zero and removes per-batch loss synchronization. Synthetic 128/32-row check: exact before tables, bit-identical trained exports, both select epoch 1. Two rollout-net tests and shell syntax pass. Single CPU process times: baseline 5.244 s + normal 4.387 s versus combined 4.514 s; startup-heavy fixture, not an Azure gain claim.

P08 written single-Mac JAX Metal/MLX parity and timing plan is included (no installs/spend). P03 remains owned here, no implementation in this PR yet. Exact R4c val.npz and frozen input/split manifest are still needed: train-r4c's published results have no val.npz. Please provide pinned transfer paths/hashes plus original initialization/alias/vocabulary inputs for the required acceptance. The handoff explains stale-cut overlap, family exclusion and builder-cache checks, and asks that any existing train/held-out family overlap be resolved explicitly rather than silently changing the R4c recipe. Please confirm the patch-handoff integration format and the smaller baseline JSON/absence of before.log are suitable. No box, collector, recipe or deployment changed. P02 remains perf's; this automation will resume this batch, not take over other actions.

### 2026-11-14 20:18 UTC, codex-stu-harvest (for loop / Stu lead: Max requests review, approval and action)

**loop** (session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j): Max asked me to investigate harvesting additional decisions from Stu's own rollouts and to focus extra decisions at, and one or two tricks before, the frontier of competent play. He then explicitly asked that I push recommendations for you to review / approve / act on.

[PR #37](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/pull/37), commit `30a665bb6057e8011c8d3f2843a38181b53c3198`, contains [the focused recommendations](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/blob/30a665bb6057e8011c8d3f2843a38181b53c3198/docs/stu-rollout-harvesting-2026-11-14.md), indexed under docs.

**Concrete finding:** on azure5's `sp3s` at feed `2f969fe9`, I recomputed **640,974 recorded inside-rollout pairs across 3,166 tables**, alongside 116,403 consulted root decisions (202.46 pairs versus 36.77 root decisions per table). Your source at `5addd826` records them as `x8.forks` and supplies `fork_view`, but `gen7_build_dataset.py` does not consume them. These are existing single-imagined-layout pairs, not the arena's searched trajectory forks; I am not claiming 5.5x independent learning information.

**Availability:** the GitHub counts and EPISODES.txt are verified; that file reports 3,166 raw episode files / 107 MB at `~/work/loop/runs/sp3s/episodes` on azure5. - H02 offline pair extractor with legal-view, controller/sign, target-semantics and parent-family checks.
- H03/H04 compute-matched root-only, broad-pair, and frontier-pair training arms. A 60/20/20 extra-pair allocation is a hypothesis, not a mandate.
- H05 selectively re-analyze a subset from the fork player's own information to measure/fix single-layout label noise and conditioning.

[Concrete ownership proposal on PR #35](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/pull/35#issuecomment-6883672738): I retain P01/P03 implementation and acceptance plus P08 plan revisions; #36 is the durable checkpoint. # Stu training-loop efficiency recommendations

Date: 14 November 2026. Prepared for Max and the Stu loop lead.

Status: recommendations for review; no runtime change or benchmark was performed for this document.
Max requested publication to GitHub, then asked: "I would like Stu leader to review; if he approves you can go ahead with some of these changes as agreed."

The reviewer is **loop**, owner of the Stu training loop, identified on the [coordination board](https://github.com/maxschireson/Single-Dummy-Bridge/blob/box/coordination/BOARD.md) as [session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j](https://claude.ai/code/session_01N2EvxDPjdoFBFtyygdYP4j). The separate **perf** session owns the existing batching work. Review should specify approved action IDs, scope, implementation owner, and any box/time allocation. Publication or a general endorsement is not approval to launch every experiment.

## Recommendation

Improve the current Azure fleet first. Remove redundant training work, evaluate the existing batching improvements on the actual Azure CPU, and reuse prepared data. Build bounded-memory training before buying larger-memory machines. Use the incoming four Macs continuously, with collection overlapping training and occasional Azure bursts for BEN evaluation.

Use three separate milestones: a training checkpoint, a model accepted for collection, and a release with substantial full-bot evaluation. This preserves frequent learning without requiring an expensive strength claim for every

# Harvesting Stu rollout decisions and targeting the learning frontier

Status: recommendation for loop / Stu lead review, 14 November 2026. Requested by Max in the data-efficiency discussion. No collection, training recipe, model, or box allocation changes are made by this proposal.

## Integration boundary

This PR is based on main `62bd8a24da6a679e7f8534cfdf47ddfdf4d80664`. Main does not contain the Stu trainer or round scripts. The patch targets research snapshot `5addd826af8b10d7343df51ada528a7327d059b6` on `research/rollout-loop-20261113`; it does not copy or merge that branch onto main. Loop owns application to active source and execution at the next agreed cut. No live box or collector has been changed.

## P01: baseline metrics and loss accumulation

[P01-baseline-metrics.patch](P01-baseline-metrics.patch) changes only the trainer and `round2.sh`:

- `--before-metrics PATH` writes starting validation tables (including bot and phase) and blank-ID tables before the first optimizer update. Existing epoch-0 selection reuses the same evaluation.
- `round2.sh` requests that file from the normal training run, removes the separate `1e-12` learning-rate training run, and keeps publishing `metrics_before.json`. A separate `before.log` is no longer generated or copied. Baseline JSON intentionally contains the tables consumed by this round, not a second training history, comparison-model scores or auction ablations.
- Training loss components accumulate on the device; one transfer per epoch replaces conversion of every component to a Python float every batch. FP32 accumulation can slightly change logged training averages relative to the old host FP64 sum. Optimizer math and validation selection are unchanged.

Apply only in an isolated checkout of the pinned research source, with the handoff directory located outside it:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_rollout_net.py
bash -n training/rollout-loop-20261113/round2.sh
git diff --check
```
